scenarios.assumptions:
The attacker starts with condition s only.
Source: Idika, N. and Bhargava, B. (2012). Extending Attack Graph-Based Security Metrics and Aggregating Their Application. IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing, 9(1), 75-85. Fig. 3 'Attack Graph Gj with vulnerabilities 1 through 13' (p. 78); Table 2 (p. 84); text on p. 84.
Transcription notes: Edges read from the embedded figure image (807x1221 px), with enlarged crops. High confidence: s->v1, s->v2, s->v3, s->v4; v2->c1; c1->v5, c1->v6, c1->v7; v5->g, v6->g, v7->g, v9->g; v3->c2; c2->v8, c2->v10; v8->c4, v10->c4; c4->v9; v4->c3->v11->c5->v12->c6->v13. Medium-high confidence: v1->g is one long straight line that passes behind v6 (it goes in at v6's upper left and comes out at its lower left, parallel to the v6->g line). I read it as v1->g, not as v1->v6, because v6 has a separate arrowed edge from c1 and the line has no arrowhead at v6. High confidence: v13->c4, because the arrowhead is at c4, so this edge points upward. s-g paths (length = exploits): s-v1-g (1); s-v2-c1-v5-g (2); s-v2-c1-v6-g (2); s-v2-c1-v7-g (2); s-v3-c2-v8-c4-v9-g (3); s-v3-c2-v10-c4-v9-g (3); s-v4-c3-v11-c5-v12-c6-v13-c4-v9-g (5). From this transcription: NP 7, SP 1, mode 2, median 2, MPL 18/7 = 2.571, SDPL (population, Eq. 7 divides by NP) = 1.178, NMPL = 2.571/7 = 0.367. Table 2 prints NP 7, SP 1, MoPL 2, MePL 2, MPL 2.5, SDPL 1.1, NMPL 0.35. NP, SP, mode and median agree, and the text on p. 84 names lengths of one, two and five exploits, which matches. MPL and SDPL differ slightly: 2.571 vs 2.5 and 1.178 vs 1.1. Seven integer path lengths cannot have a mean of exactly 2.5 (that needs a sum of 17.5), so the table seems to truncate to one decimal. NMPL 0.35 equals 2.5/7 = 0.357 truncated, i.e. it was computed from the truncated MPL. I see no edge reading that gives exactly the table values; the transcription was not changed to fit them. Baseline minimum cost 1 = the paper's SP(Gj) = 1 via s, v1, g (p. 78). The 'v1 patched' scenario is my own; there v5, v6 and v7 tie (cost 2) and v2+v5 is listed.

semantics: Conditions are persistent Boolean facts; there are no delete effects or negation.
AND requires all incoming inputs; OR requires at least one. Unlabelled joins use the per-scenario AND/OR choice.
An action is enabled when its inputs hold (or it is an approved entry action); executing it assumes success.
Each action executes at most once; efforts are nonnegative, additive, and shared actions are charged once.
Minimum effort is an exact search over closed active sets; limits yield an incomplete result, never a minimum or unreachability.
importDefaults: New imports: root and declared starting conditions true; root actions allowed as entries.
New imports: unlabelled joins default to OR; missing efforts default to 1; goal = reachable node of greatest minimum dependency depth.
